core_obligations: Part (1), injectivity and surjectivity (proof lines 5223-5227): the filtration step of a subobject is the intersection of the subobject with the filtration step of the ambient object, which makes the displayed map on graded pieces injective, and dually the map from the ambient object to the quotient is surjective.

Part (1), exactness in the middle (proof lines 5228-5230): the kernel of the displayed map between graded pieces is computed to be exactly the image of the graded piece of the subobject, which is the remaining exactness.
Part (2) (proof line 5231): the two short exact sequences for the kernel, coimage, image and cokernel of a morphism are special cases of the sequence of part (1).
proof_roadmap: Compute the filtration steps of a subobject as an intersection.
Derive injectivity, surjectivity and exactness in the middle.
Specialize to the kernel, coimage, image and cokernel of a morphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces short exact sequences of graded pieces, first for a subobject of a filtered object and then for the kernel, coimage, image and cokernel of a morphism of filtered objects (statement lines 5198-5221). The proof is a complete argument: the filtration step of a subobject is identified as an intersection, which gives injectivity of the first displayed map and, dually, surjectivity of the second (proof lines 5223-5227); the kernel of the middle map is then computed to be the graded piece of the subobject, which gives exactness (proof lines 5228-5230); and the assertion about a morphism follows as a special case (proof line 5231). The non-formal content is the computation of the kernel in the middle. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
